notes: Direct fetch of course.mlsafety.org was blocked by the network egress proxy (EGRESS_BLOCKED), and web.archive.org was also unreachable. The list was instead extracted verbatim from the site's source repository, github.com/centerforaisafety/course.mlsafety.org (file readings.md; latest commit ba42d89, 2026-01-28), which is the live Jekyll source for course.mlsafety.org (CNAME confirms) — so this reflects the current published Readings page exactly. The page states: 'Italicized resources are required, and other resources are suggested' — mapped to core:true (required) vs core:false (suggested/recommended). Sections here follow the readings page's own heading hierarchy (17 subsections numbered 1-17 in page order); the course's lecture schedule (from the _modules files) groups them into 7 modules: Background (Introduction, Deep Learning Review), Safety Engineering (Risk Decomposition, Accident Models, Black Swans — the 'Risk Analysis' readings), Robustness (Adversarial Robustness, Black Swan Robustness), Monitoring (Anomaly Detection, Interpretable Uncertainty, Transparency, Trojans, Detecting Emergent Behavior), Control (Honest Models, Power Aversion, Machine Ethics), Systemic Safety (ML for Improved Decision-Making, ML for Cyberdefense, Cooperative AI), and Additional Existential Risk Discussion. The readings page shows no authors or years; authors/years supplied here come from the papers themselves (years for arXiv items derived from arXiv IDs) — treat non-arXiv years/authors marked null as not stated. PixMix appears twice on the page (Long Tails and Interpretable Uncertainty) and is listed under both. The 'Introduction to STAMP' entry has both a video and a slides URL, and the Croce & Hein AutoAttack entry links robustbench.github.io — captured in extra_urls. The three risk-engineering.org links share one bullet on the page but are listed as three entries. No other course page (schedule/calendar/modules) contains additional reading links; module pages link only lecture videos, slides, course notes, assignments, and Colab notebooks.
